svg.title: Evidence layers for five studies published on 28 August 2026
svg.desc: A map separating physical experiments from numerical evidence for Gibbs-state preparation, two-dimensional XY analog simulation, organic-semiconductor exciton spectroscopy, fluxonium-transmon architecture, and geometric pulse control
svg.text: Published together, but not the same kind of evidence
Interpret the result only after locating what was executed or measured.

g.text: CLASSICAL NUMERICS
Gibbs thermal-state preparation
Resettable bath + modulated coupling · 2D Ising to 16 spins · free fermions to hundreds of sites
No QPU run, reset overhead, mixing time, or end-to-end wall-clock measurement
ANALOG EXPERIMENT
2D XY spin diffusion
Optical-lattice hard-core-boson simulator · experimental D = 0.82(3)J · agreement with Dyn-HTE
Not a universal digital QPU or a speedup demonstration over classical computation
SPECTROSCOPY
α-sexithiophene exciton
Momentum space measured · real-space amplitude and phase reconstructed · coherent over ~3 molecules
A ~25% contraction within 400 fs supports self-trapping but does not uniquely prove its cause
CLOSED-SYSTEM SIM.
Fluxonium–transmon architecture
Fluxonium data qubit · transmon measurement ancilla · tunable coupler
CZ results at ≥30 ns are simulated, not measured chip fidelity, array yield, or logical error rate
THEORY + NUMERICS
Geometric diabatic–adiabatic pulses
Allow target transitions while suppressing multilevel leakage · one control → first-order ODE
No fidelity measured on a pulse generator or spin-qubit device

svg.text: Judge evidence by execution site, measured quantity, and baseline—not publication alone.
